ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two flat strips of paper, each with a width of 1, are overlaid in a cross fashion. The angle between the edges of the two strips is $\alpha =30^\circ$. What is the area of their overlapping part (the shaded area in the figure)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure: Draw AE$\perp$BC and AF$\perp$CD at F, with the feet of the perpendiculars being E and F,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AEB=$\angle$AFD=$90^\circ$,\\
$\because$AD$\parallel$CB and AB$\parallel$CD,\\
$\therefore$quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,\\
$\because$the width of the strip is 1,\\
$\therefore$AE=AF=1,\\
In $\triangle$ABE and $\triangle$ADF\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle ABE=\angle ADF=30^\circ \\
\angle AEB=\angle AFD=90^\circ \\
AE=AF
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ABE$\cong$ $\triangle$ADF (AAS),\\
$\therefore$AB=AD,\\
$\therefore$quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus.\\
$\therefore$BC=AB,\\
$\because$ $\frac{AE}{AB}=\sin 30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$BC=AB=$\frac{1}{\sin 30^\circ}=2$,\\
$\therefore$the area of the overlapping part (the shaded area in the figure) is: BC×AE=2×1=\boxed{2},

method.method_draft: Analytic coordinate/Jacobian route. First read the diagram: the overlap is the intersection of a horizontal strip with a slanted strip, and the angle between their edge directions is alpha. From the text, both strip widths are 1 and alpha = 30 degrees. Place coordinates so the horizontal strip is 0 <= y <= 1. Describe the slanted strip by its signed perpendicular coordinate v, where v = -sin(alpha)x + cos(alpha)y; because the slanted strip has width 1, it is 0 <= v <= 1 after choosing the origin on one slanted edge. The shaded overlap is therefore the set of points whose two strip-normal coordinates satisfy 0 <= y <= 1 and 0 <= v <= 1. The map (x,y) -> (u,v) with u=y and v=-sin(alpha)x+cos(alpha)y sends the overlap to the unit square 0 <= u <= 1, 0 <= v <= 1. Its determinant has absolute value sin(alpha), so area in the original plane equals unit-square area divided by sin(alpha). Thus the overlap area is 1/sin 30 degrees = 2.

solver_metadata.cot_raw: 图像描述：图中可见两条等宽纸带交叉重叠：一条纸带近似水平，另一条纸带斜向穿过它；中间阴影部分是两条纸带的公共重叠区域，形状为平行四边形。图中右上方标出斜纸带边缘与水平纸带边缘之间的夹角为 α，题设给出 α = 30°，两条纸带的宽度均为 1。推理：按解析坐标/Jacobian 方法，令水平纸带为 0 ≤ y ≤ 1。斜纸带的边缘方向与水平线夹角为 α，因此取它的法向 signed coordinate 为 v = -sin(α)x + cos(α)y。由于斜纸带宽度为 1，可选取原点位置使斜纸带对应 0 ≤ v ≤ 1。于是阴影重叠区域正是满足 0 ≤ y ≤ 1 且 0 ≤ v ≤ 1 的点集。令 u = y，则映射 (x,y) -> (u,v) = (y, -sin(α)x + cos(α)y) 把重叠区域映到单位正方形 0 ≤ u ≤ 1, 0 ≤ v ≤ 1。该线性变换的 Jacobian 行列式绝对值为 sin(α)，所以原平面面积 = uv 平面单位正方形面积 / sin(α) = 1 / sin(30°) = 1 / (1/2) = 2。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, two flat strips of paper, each with a width of 1, are overlaid in a cross fashion. The angle between the edges of the two strips is $\alpha = 30^\circ$. What is the area of their overlapping part (the shaded area in the figure)?
raw_record.answer: Solution: As shown in the figure, draw AE$\perp$BC and AF$\perp$CD at F, with the feet of the perpendiculars being E and F. Therefore $\angle$AEB = $\angle$AFD = $90^\circ$. Because AD$\parallel$CB and AB$\parallel$CD, quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram. Because the width of the strip is 1, AE = AF = 1. In $\triangle$ABE and $\triangle$ADF, $\angle$ABE = $\angle$ADF = $30^\circ$, $\angle$AEB = $\angle$AFD = $90^\circ$, and AE = AF, so $\triangle$ABE $\cong$ $\triangle$ADF (AAS). Therefore AB = AD, so quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus. Hence BC = AB. Because $\frac{AE}{AB} = \sin 30^\circ$, we get BC = AB = $\frac{1}{\sin 30^\circ} = 2$. Therefore the area of the overlapping part is BC $\times$ AE = 2 $\times$ 1 = $\boxed{2}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, there are two paper strips of the same width crossed and stacked, one paper strip is approximately horizontal, and the other paper strip passes through it obliquely. The shaded overlapping part is quadrilateral ABCD, where BC and AD are respectively on the two parallel edges of the horizontal paper strip, and AB and CD are respectively on the two parallel edges of the oblique paper strip. In the figure, angle α is marked near D, indicating the acute angle between the horizontal edge and the oblique edge; the problem gives α=30°, and the width of each paper strip is 1.
Reasoning: Because the two pairs of opposite sides of ABCD respectively come from the parallel edges of the two paper strips, ABCD is a parallelogram. Take the horizontal edge BC as the base, then the height of this parallelogram relative to BC is exactly the width of the horizontal paper strip, namely the height is 1. The base BC is, in the horizontal-edge direction, the distance between the two oblique paper-strip edges. The perpendicular distance between the two edges of the oblique paper strip is its width 1; they make an angle of 30° with the horizontal direction, so if the horizontal spacing is BC, then BC·sin30°=1. Therefore BC=1/sin30°=1/(1/2)=2. Overlapping area=base×height=BC×1=2×1=2.
